text: The prospect says the price is too high for their current budget. Recommended response: acknowledge the budget constraint, connect the product to the cost of the manual work it replaces, and propose starting with the team or workflow where measurable payback will be fastest before discussing a broader rollout.

The prospect says they need to think about it. Recommended response: respect the decision process, ask what specifically they need to evaluate, and offer to resolve that one open concern with a short proof point or stakeholder conversation rather than applying pressure.

The prospect says they already have a tool that does this. Recommended response: agree that replacing a working tool may not be necessary, then ask which outcomes or workflows remain difficult and position Kairos around those gaps instead of claiming the incumbent is inadequate.

The prospect is concerned that implementation will take too long. Recommended response: outline the phased onboarding plan, identify the first low-risk workflow, and explain what Kairos handles for them so the evaluation focuses on time to first value rather than a theoretical full migration.

The prospect says their data is too sensitive to put into a new platform. Recommended response: ask about the exact data classification and security requirements, explain the available access controls and retention options, and offer a security review with the right technical owner before asking for production data.

The prospect says they do not have enough internal resources to run a pilot. Recommended response: narrow the pilot to one owner, one workflow, and a small set of success criteria, then provide a concrete enablement checklist so the team can validate value without creating a second project to manage.

The prospect wants a custom feature before moving forward. Recommended response: clarify the business outcome behind the request, show how the current product handles the core use case, and document the feature for roadmap review without making an uncommitted delivery promise.

The prospect says they need approval from legal and procurement. Recommended response: ask for the approval criteria and timeline, provide the standard security and contract materials early, and align on a mutual action plan that keeps the business champion involved while those reviews happen.

The prospect is worried that users will not adopt another workflow. Recommended response: validate the adoption concern, demonstrate the fewest-click path for the target users, and agree on an adoption measure and feedback loop so the pilot proves behavior change rather than just technical connectivity.
